title: Vuln evidence compact export and RBACv2 onboarding notes
body:
Purpose:
This working note captures a compact export format for vulnerability evidence ingestion into SIEM and the RBACv2 onboarding checklist needed to ensure evidence access controls. Target audience: SecOps, SRE, Platform, and the Evidence Automation engineers. This is a living document — intended as the operational handoff for the export schema, automation steps, and the immediate onboarding tasks for RBACv2 rollout in vuln workflows.

Scope:
- Compact SIEM export of vulnerability findings and associated evidence pointers (not full payloads) for retention and alerting.
- Audit log schema additions required to link scanner output -> remediation ticket -> evidence artifacts.
- RBACv2 onboarding checklist for teams/roles that need evidence read/write/delete.
- Patch SLA definitions and how to expose SLA state in exports.
- Implementation notes for evidence automation (S3 paths, signing, retention, replay).

Background / problem statement:
Our current vulnerability exports to SIEM are bulky (full JSON blobs) and cause indexing cost and retention bloat in Splunk/Elastic. We want a compact, normalized export that keeps the minimal fields required for alerting/correlation and keeps heavy artifacts (logs, full scanner JSON) as references (S3/archival store). Concurrently RBACv2 rollout changes role names and bindings; we need to ensure the new role attributes propagate into audit logs so SecOps can query who accessed evidence.

Design goals:
- Compactness: <= 1KB per record typical (NDJSON line).
- Traceability: every SIEM row must include a stable trace_id to join to archival evidence.
- Access-aware: include actor_role_v2 or role_hash so RBAC filters can be applied in queries.
- Tamper-evidence: signed evidence pointers (HMAC) and optional audit_hash field.
- Backward compatibility: support legacy exports for 90 days during migration.

Compact SIEM export schema (NDJSON line) - proposed fields and examples:
- event_id: stable UUID for SIEM event (string)
- trace_id: stable identifier across systems (scanner run id + vuln id) (string)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC (string)
- scanner: enumerated (trivy|grype|snyk|sca-producer) (string)
- vuln_id: canonical vuln id (CVE or internal) (string)
- severity: one of critical|high|medium|low|info (string)
- resource_type: e.g., container_image|lambda|repo_dependency|k8s_cluster (string)
- resource_id: stable resource identifier (image sha, repo@rev, cluster:id) (string)
- fix_available: boolean string (true|false)
- patch_sla_state: e.g., open|in_progress|mitigated|waived|deferred (string)
- patch_sla_days_left: integer as string (number of days)
- evidence_s3_path: s3 path to zipped evidence (s3://redwood-vuln-evidence/prod/2026-11/traceid.zip) (string)
- evidence_signature: base64 HMAC of the artifact (string)
- actor_id: if scanner triggered via CI, actor (system:user) (string)
- actor_role_v2: RBACv2 role label or hashed role (string)
- audit_hash: short hash of event fields (for tamper detection) (string)
- indexed_tags: comma-separated quick tags for SIEM (string)

Example NDJSON line (one line):
{"event_id":"6f8a9d2e-3a4a-4c9f-a8d4-1e2b3c4d5f6a","trace_id":"scanner-20261115-57b3-vuln-2026-0471","timestamp":"2026-11-15T14:22:05Z","scanner":"trivy","vuln_id":"CVE-2026-0471","severity":"high","resource_type":"container_image","resource_id":"gcr.io/redwood/service-a@sha256:abcd1234","fix_available":"true","patch_sla_state":"open","patch_sla_days_left":"6","evidence_s3_path":"s3://redwood-vuln-evidence/prod/2026-11/scanner-20261115-57b3-vuln-2026-0471.zip","evidence_signature":"b64:...","actor_id":"ci:github-actions","actor_role_v2":"rbacv2:scanner-service:readonly","audit_hash":"sha256:1a2b3c","indexed_tags":"k8s,prod,service-a"}

CSV export (compact) header example for teams that prefer CSV ingestion into legacy tools:
event_id,trace_id,timestamp,scanner,vuln_id,severity,resource_type,resource_id,fix_available,patch_sla_state,patch_sla_days_left,evidence_s3_path,actor_id,actor_role_v2,indexed_tags

Audit log schema additions (to support traceability and RBACv2):
- audit_event_id (string) - unique per audit row
- related_trace_ids (csv string) - trace ids referenced
- actor_id (string)
- actor_role_v2 (string) - canonical role label from RBACv2 (e.g., sec.read_evidence)
- action (string) - read_evidence|download_evidence|delete_evidence|update_metadata|create_evidence
- resource_type / resource_id (string)
- audit_timestamp (ISO8601)
- outcome (success|failure|forbidden|error)
- evidence_pointer (s3 path or internal id)
- event_signature (base64) - HMAC over (actor_id + timestamp + resource_id) to detect tamper
- session_id (optional) - ephemeral session for elevated access

RBACv2 onboarding checklist (operational tasks) - for each team that needs evidence access:
1) Inventory roles: list existing roles that currently have vuln evidence access. Map to RBACv2 role names. (owner: Priya)
2) Define least-privilege role labels: evidence.viewer, evidence.downloader, evidence.admin, evidence.writer.
3) Create role-bindings for service accounts used by scanners and automation: scanner-service -> evidence.writer (only write to evidence bucket prefix).
4) Ensure read-only roles map to evidence.viewer and cannot generate new traces or delete artifacts.
5) Temporary elevated access flow: implement one-click request in Console -> requires justification, duration, approver. Logs must include session_id and approver_id in audit log.
6) Verify role propagation in audit logs: sample query (below) must return actor_role_v2 for recent events.
7) Update runbooks and run an onboarding exercise with two volunteer teams (SRE + Platform) to confirm access matrix.

RBACv2 audit verification sample Splunk query (conceptual):
index="vuln-audit" actor_role_v2="*evidence*" | stats count by actor_id, actor_role_v2, action, outcome | where outcome!="success"

Evidence automation pipeline (high-level steps):
- trigger: scanner run completes in CI or periodic scheduled job.
- produce: normalized artifact bundle (minimal JSON + zipped logs + scanner-full.json).
- sign: HMAC with evidence service key (KMS-backed).
- store: upload to s3://redwood-vuln-evidence/<env>/<YYYY-MM>/<trace_id>.zip
- index: write compact NDJSON line to SIEM export stream (Kafka topic: vuln-export-compact) and to internal audit DB (Dynamo/Postgres).
- notify: fire webhook to ticketing system (Jira SEC-xxxx) with trace_id and evidence pointer.
- retention: short-term: 90 days on hot S3; cold archive: Glacier deep archive after 1 year; retention TTL configured in bucket lifecycle.
- replay: automation service can rehydrate artifacts for forensic requests; replay requests should require evidence.viewer+session request logged.

S3 naming / partitioning conventions (operational):
- s3://redwood-vuln-evidence/<env>/<year>-<month>/<scanner>/<trace_id>.zip
- metadata sidecar: <trace_id>.meta.json (contains manifest, audit_hash, signing info)
- example: s3://redwood-vuln-evidence/prod/2026-11/trivy/scanner-20261115-57b3-vuln-2026-0471.zip

Patch SLA definitions (proposal):
- P0 / Critical: action within 24 hours; automated mitigation where possible (block, emergency patch).
- P1 / High: owner assigned within 24 hours, full remediation or validated mitigation within 7 days.
- P2 / Medium: remediation within 30 days.
- P3 / Low: remediation within 90 days or documented waiver.
- Waiver process: ticket must include business rationale, compensating controls, and approved by SecEng lead. Waivers recorded as patch_sla_state=waived and waiver_id.

Exposing SLA state in exports:
- patch_sla_state and patch_sla_days_left fields shown above. Systems consuming the compact export should use these to escalate. Patch SLA state transitions should be emitted as events (patch-sla-change) so SIEM rules can alert for P0/P1 misses.

Remediation tracking states (internal canonical states):
- new -> triaged -> in_progress -> awaiting_validation -> mitigated -> closed -> waived -> deferred
- Each transition must store actor_id and timestamp. If transition is automated (CI remediation), actor_id=automation:remediator and actor_role_v2=rbacv2:automation:writer.

Testing plan for rollout (minimum required):
- Unit tests: serializer/deserializer for compact format, HMAC signing tests.
- Integration tests: end-to-end scanner run (staging), evidence upload, SIEM ingestion check (index count), and audit row created with actor_role_v2 present.
- Load test: simulate 10k vuln events/day to confirm NDJSON stream and SIEM indexing cost estimate.
- Backfill: run compact export for last 3 months in staging and compare counts to legacy export.

Operational runbook extracts (quick):
- How to locate evidence for trace_id: use internal tool https://tools.redwood.ai/evidence?trace_id=<id> or S3 direct lookup.
- If evidence not found: check automation logs (GitHub Actions run id), check upload lambda metrics, check KMS permissions (kms:Encrypt on evidence key).
- If audit logs missing actor_role_v2: likely RBACv2 propagation issue; file JIRA 'SEC-ONBOARD-<team>' and tag #sec-vuln-ops.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical max NDJSON size threshold (should we compress per line?).
- Confirm whether we want to include partial stack traces in evidence meta or leave them only in archived scanner-full.json.
- Define SLA exception labeling schema and where that is stored (ticket vs. evidence meta).
- Authorization model for replaying archived evidence (team approvals vs. automated service).

Appendix A: useful internal refs and tickets:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Vuln+Evidence+Standards
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-8123 (rbacv2 rollout), JIRA-SEC-8230 (evidence-bucket-iam), JIRA-SEC-8299 (siem-compact-export)
- Github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/vuln-evidence-automation/pulls
- Slack channels: #sec-vuln-ops, #platform-automation, #sre-oncall

Appendix B: sample Splunk/Elastic queries (operational recipes)
- Splunk: index=vuln-compact patch_sla_state="open" severity="high" | stats count by resource_id, patch_sla_days_left | where patch_sla_days_left<3
- Elastic (KQL): event.dataset:vuln-compact and patch_sla_state:"open" and severity:"high" | group_by resource_id | where patch_sla_days_left < 3

Contact / next steps:
- Owners: Mariana Lopez (sec-ops lead), Priya Nair (evidence automation), Ethan Kim (platform infra).
- Next sync: 2026-11-24 10:00 PT — run onboarding dry-run with SRE volunteers.
- Deliverables before sync: implementation PR for compact export (PR #47), sample NDJSON dump of 100 events, RBACv2 mapping doc for two pilot teams.

Notes to self (informal):
- keep compact but include everything to triage quickly; avoid over-indexing whole scanner JSON.
- ensure hash/signing keys rotate monthly and are in KMS.
- coordinate with Billing on estimated SIEM index cost savings (this drives the business case).

Last edited by Mariana Lopez on 2026-11-21 (draft).
